summary: This sermon unpacks the theological term 'Christoformity,' which means being conformed to the image of Christ. The speaker argues that the goal of salvation is not merely getting to heaven but being transformed into the likeness of Jesus in every area of life, both now and for eternity.
key_points: Christoformity is being predestined and shaped to reflect Jesus' life, ministry, death, and resurrection
Knowing Jesus through Scripture, especially the Gospels, is essential to being formed like Him
Transformation happens in community—no one is conformed to Christ alone
The Christian life involves ongoing obedience, confession, and repentance, not just a one-time decision
Communion is the central practice that both remembers and re-members us into Christ's body
big_idea: The ultimate purpose of the Christian life is Christoformity—being completely reshaped into the image of Jesus through the Spirit's work in community with His body, the church.
title: Christoformity
